records.c: Jump to the scoreboard runtime at $B253. The resident caller passes the data length, source address and continuation address immediately after its JSR at $2C88.
Zero-terminated strings used by the first display row. They include the pins heading, the multiplication sign, zero suffixes and the result arrow.
Zero-terminated captions and operators for the objects score row, selected by the descriptor group at $B471.
Text and formatting strings for the music score row, referenced from the layout records at $B4B1.
Captions, operators and literal zero suffixes for the completed-towers row.
The countdown label and the punctuation between its three time fields.
Title and literal zero suffix used by the final score row.
Enter the frame containing the integer-to-text formatter through the descriptor at $A5BB.
Frame descriptor read by $B2AF from after the JSR at $A5B8. Save 2 working bytes from zero page $30 and add 0 to the software stack pointer before entering $A5BE.
Allocate and build a null-terminated decimal string on the temporary output buffer. The caller passes the output length and its value through the frame argument area.
First callback index after the scoreboard finishes, taken from offset four after the resident JSR's return address.
Second callback index, from offset five. Used after the scene-data copy at $A70B.

Read the resident call's inline parameters and copy the supplied values and function pointers into the local table at $B360. Apply the scoreboard palette, invoke its asset-loader callback twice and import the saved score block when the marker is $77.
Fetch the resident resource-loader callback from $B36B/$B36C and tail-call it with the index still in X.
Fetch the callback address from $B36F/$B370 and pass it to the indirect dispatcher.
Fetch the address from $B373/$B374 and transfer to it through $000A.
Form a little-endian pointer at $0A/$0B from A and Y and jump through it without creating a new return address.
A single RTS opcode sits between the unconditional indirect jump at $A73A and the next entry at $A73E. The dispatcher transfers control before reaching this byte.
Fill colour RAM with 9 across four pages. Select screen $F000 and character set $C000, enable multicolour characters and set black background with cyan and blue multicolour values.
Writable high address byte of the colour-fill store at $A744. Each 256-byte pass increments it to the next colour page.

Pull the call site, read the two entry-count bytes and scan its four-byte records for an exact match with $0A/$0B. Jump through the matching destination or the default address preceding the first record.
Copy X pages plus Y bytes backward from ($7E) to ($80), adjusting each pointer high byte as the copy crosses pages.
Enter the tally routine through the descriptor at $A7F1, which saves two zero-page work bytes.
Frame descriptor read by $B2AF from after the JSR at $A7EE. Save 2 working bytes from zero page $30 and add 0 to the software stack pointer before entering $A7F4.

Multiply the four category counts by their weights at $B429 and following, then place the products in the fields at $B41A–$B423. Use the remaining-time fields in the score calculation, sum the category values and prepare the numeric output fields.
Five periods followed by a string terminator, used as the default name template.
Open the local frame that holds a sequential score-layout table pointer and record index.
Frame descriptor read by $B2AF from after the JSR at $AAD1. Save 6 working bytes from zero page $30 and add -4 to the software stack pointer before entering $AAD7.

Iterate 45 eight-byte descriptors at $B431. Set the screen column, row and colour, draw the optional zero-terminated caption and then format the requested number of digits from the descriptor's value pointer.
Two literal zero characters and a terminator, printed after a stored score entry's formatted value.
Call the scoreboard frame helper to reserve working bytes for a string pointer.
Frame descriptor read by $B2AF from after the JSR at $AC5B. Save 2 working bytes from zero page $30 and add 0 to the software stack pointer before entering $AC61.
Read the string pointer from the arguments. For each nonzero byte push its character and the current cursor coordinates to $AF29, then advance the column. Zero finishes the string.
Call the frame helper for the rewind prompt and subsequent key wait.
Frame descriptor read by $B2AF from after the JSR at $ACAE. Save 0 working bytes from zero page $30 and add 0 to the software stack pointer before entering $ACB4.
Print the padded REWIND AND PLAY message at row 15 and column 3. Poll $B06D until it reports a key.
Null-terminated PETSCII text with trailing spaces to replace the rest of the score display row.
Enter name editing through the descriptor at $AD01, reserving two local bytes after the zero-page save.
Frame descriptor read by $B2AF from after the JSR at $ACFE. Save 4 working bytes from zero page $30 and add -2 to the software stack pointer before entering $AD04.

Position the name cursor by the score-table entry index. Accept uppercase A–Z and Return, limit the cursor to the selected entry's extent and update both the name bytes and screen. The exact-key dispatcher at $AF12 selects editing actions for other accepted keys.
If the name cursor is past the first column, restore the departed cell's colour and decrement the column.
If the next column is inside the name field, restore the departed cell's colour and increment the column.
If the cursor can back up, decrement it, write a period into the selected name record and redraw that character in the high-score row.
Exact-dispatch table for Delete, cursor right and cursor left. It has a two-byte count, default target and three four-byte key-and-address records.
Re-enter the name editor's keyboard loop at $ADAE after a cursor or delete action.
Enter the character writer with two saved zero-page work bytes.
Frame descriptor read by $B2AF from after the JSR at $AF29. Save 2 working bytes from zero page $30 and add 0 to the software stack pointer before entering $AF2F.
Normalize the input through $B14A, convert digits to the corresponding display codes and dispatch the supported punctuation characters. Use the row and column arguments to locate the screen cell.
Convert PETSCII space to screen glyph zero, then join the cell writer.
Select score glyph $28 for the multiplication mark.
Select score glyph $27 for the period.
Select score glyph $29 for the greater-than or arrow mark.
Select score glyph $25 for the question mark.
Select score glyph $26 for the exclamation mark.
Six four-byte code-and-target records, with count and default address. The table handles space, exclamation, star, period, greater-than and question mark.
Compute the row-major screen cell from row times 40 plus column. Write the selected glyph to the scoreboard's character map.
Enter the string-copy routine through the four-byte workspace frame at $B022.
Frame descriptor read by $B2AF from after the JSR at $B01F. Save 4 working bytes from zero page $30 and add 0 to the software stack pointer before entering $B025.
Copy source bytes to the destination pointer and advance both words. The final zero is copied to the output together with the text.
Use the frame helper before polling the program's ROM keyboard service.
Frame descriptor read by $B2AF from after the JSR at $B06D. Save 0 working bytes from zero page $30 and add 0 to the software stack pointer before entering $B073.

Expose the KERNAL, clear the keyboard buffer count, reset the last matrix key and scan with $EA87. Use the next byte if it differs from the saved input at $B0AB, otherwise return zero. Restore all-RAM game banking on exit.
One zero byte between the keyboard routine's return at $B0A9 and its saved key at $B0AB.
Last effective PETSCII value read from the keyboard buffer. $B073 clears it when no key is buffered.
Open a local frame for the row and column arguments.
Frame descriptor read by $B2AF from after the JSR at $B0AD. Save 2 working bytes from zero page $30 and add 0 to the software stack pointer before entering $B0B3.
Compute the colour RAM address as $D800 plus 40 times row plus column. When column is below 37, increment the cell's colour by one.
Open a local frame for the addressed cursor cell.
Frame descriptor read by $B2AF from after the JSR at $B0FE. Save 2 working bytes from zero page $30 and add 0 to the software stack pointer before entering $B104.
Compute the same row-major colour RAM address and write $B430 to its cell if the column is below 37.
Enter the character normalizer through an empty frame descriptor.
Frame descriptor read by $B2AF from after the JSR at $B14A. Save 0 working bytes from zero page $30 and add 0 to the software stack pointer before entering $B150.
For values strictly above $40, set bit 5 in the argument. Return the resulting byte in $0A and clear the high result at $0B.
Multiply the word in zero page indexed by Y by the word in X:A through the shift-and-add loop. Keep the low 16 bits of the result in the original indexed pair.
Normalize operand signs, divide the positive magnitudes and restore the quotient sign in the destination word.
Normalize operand signs, calculate the remainder and restore the sign according to the original dividend.
Divide an indexed 16-bit zero-page value by X:A, using a 16-step shift, compare and subtract loop. Return quotient in the original pair and remainder at $02/$03.
Clear the two-byte remainder then shift and conditionally subtract the divisor 16 times. Store the quotient in the indexed work pair.
Save the dividend sign and the quotient sign derived from both operands. Negate negative magnitudes before the unsigned division loop.
Shift the zero-page word indexed by Y left by the count in X:A. Return with an empty X:A result and Y one after updating the word.
Clear decimal mode and set RAM banking, pull the resident return address into $B382/$B383 and initialize the software stack at $023F before switching the hardware stack to $FF.

The scoreboard's copy of the resident range dispatch. Use the pulled call address to add the first inline word to the selector; compare with the second and use the default or indexed destination word accordingly.

Save the previous software-frame pointers and the requested zero-page working bytes, then enter the code following the call's inline frame descriptor. Install synthetic return address $B31E so RTS restores the working frame.
Restore the saved work bytes and software stack, undo the inline descriptor's requested hardware-stack allocation and jump to the original continuation.
Start of the caller-supplied structure copied from $238C. It carries scores, countdown fields and callback pointers.
Second countdown field supplied by the resident. Reset at $A881 when the first time field exceeds 127.
Third countdown field from the caller, moved to the working pair at $B418.
Low byte of the pins count passed to the first weighted product at $A807.
High byte of the caller's pins count, loaded into $1B at $A7FC.
Low byte of the objects count used by the second multiplication.
High byte of the objects count placed in $1B at $A81C.
Low byte of the completed-tower count, paired with weight 20.
High byte paired with the tower count read by $A854.
Low byte of the music count used with the third weight.
High byte of the count multiplied at $A847 for the music row.
Low byte of the indirect tape-resource target built by $A71B and $A736.
High byte of the resident tape-resource callback used by $A71B.
Low byte of the callback target that $A724 dispatches through the zero-page pointer.
High byte of the callback target loaded into Y at $A727.
Load index passed to the resident callback's first invocation by $A68A.
Load index used by the following callback at $A693.
Low byte of the indirect continuation selected by $A72D after the scoreboard.
High byte of the resident continuation selected by the scoreboard's restart path.
When the caller sets this byte, $A69B checks for the $77 marker and conditionally copies 96 saved score bytes.
Temporary digit buffer used by the decimal formatter. Output strings terminate with zero so the renderer can stop.
The numeric formatter selects PETSCII zero at $AB61 or space at $AB69 before drawing the value field.
The layout initialization at $AADF and name-entry setup at $AD22 both save Y to this byte.
Entry $B253 removes the resident return address from the hardware stack and stores its low byte here for the inline-parameter reader.
Saved high byte of the resident return address used at $A657 to make the parameter pointer.
The layout initializer stores X here at $AAE5. The name editor resets the same byte at $AD25.
Adjacent byte also written from X during layout setup, at $AAE2, and name-entry setup, at $AD28.
PETSCII instruction to press any key to restart.
PETSCII prompt printed above the high-score entry cells.

Twelve score records of eight bytes each. Every default row starts with a five-character dotted placeholder followed by three zero bytes. $A653 restores all 96 bytes from $A480 when the save marker matches.
Hand-over values for score-state and display scratch fields between the stored name table and the numeric subtotal fields.
The first caller-supplied time byte, copied into a word before the time calculation.
The tally clears the high byte of the first time field before reading the pair in the time calculation at $A8AD.
Set by the accepted-letter path at $ADFD. After the rewind prompt returns, $A6CE tests it before copying the 96-byte table back to the resident.
Low byte copied from $B361 and used as the second input to the time calculation.
Cleared high byte of the second time field, fetched at $A8C5.
Low byte copied from $B362 by the tally code at $A89E.
Cleared high byte paired with the third time field at $B418.
Low byte of the product of pins count and the first weight, stored at $A80C.
High byte of the first category product, stored at $A811.
Low byte written at $A82C after multiplying the objects count by two.
High byte of the object product read with the low byte during total calculation.
Low byte of the third product. The music row layout reads this subtotal from its address.
High byte fetched from the multiplication result at $A84F.
Low byte of the total formed at $A939. The high-score scan compares this byte against the low byte in each recorded score.
High byte of the total, stored after propagating carry from the sum's low byte.
Low byte of the product of the tower count and weight 20.
High byte of the tower product, read by the high-byte addition at $A931.
Low byte of the combined time fields divided by 100. The alternate path at $A901 clears it.
High byte of the time subtotal, added to the other products at $A941.
Initially 12, the index beyond the end of the table. Replaced at $A99D if the new total fits and used by the name editor to choose a record.
High byte of the insertion index checked together with its low byte by the signed comparisons.
Cleared from X immediately before the tally call at $A6B7.
Low byte of the first multiplier, 1, used by the pins calculation.
High byte of the first multiplier, loaded into X before the pins multiplication.
Low byte of the second multiplier, 2, used by the objects calculation.
High byte of the second multiplier loaded at $A81E.
Low byte of the third multiplier, 3, used by the music calculation.
High byte of the third multiplier moved into X before $A847.
Column shared between the score renderer and the name editor. The letter-writing path at $AE2E advances it after a character.
The renderer updates this byte while iterating descriptors. The name editor's restore routine copies it back to the selected cell.
Eight display descriptors for the pins row. Each record contains column, row, caption address, numeric address, digit count and colour.
Eight descriptors for the objects row. Its values refer to the count at $B365, weight at $B42B and subtotal at $B41C.
Eight descriptors for the music row. Numeric address $B41E selects that row's subtotal.
Eight descriptors for the tower row, including the completed-towers label and the value pointer at $B422.
Nine descriptors for the time-remaining row. Individual numeric fields and punctuation are interleaved before the subtotal.
Four descriptors for the Your Score row and the restart prompt below it. The total field uses four digits before the literal suffix.
Low byte selected at $AAB5 or $AAC2. It points to the name prompt when the score enters the table and to the restart message otherwise.
Common high byte $B3 of the two possible message addresses supplied to the scoreboard layout.
Current row for the score screen's character writer and for name-entry cursor drawing.
Low byte of the $0014 multiplier used with the count at $B367 during the tally routine's fourth product.
High byte of that weight, read by $A85E and transferred to X before the multiplication call at $A867.
The final 340 bytes of tape record 664 alternate long $FF and zero runs. Read, write and execute watches registered zero accesses between scoreboard entry at $A520 and the name-entry poll at $ADAE.
